TALMIND

Age:

Middle school.

Required equipment

Every student has a tablet and headphones with a microphone

The structure of the curriculum - includes 3 stages:

  1. 1

    Introductory video (2 - 5 minutes).

  2. 2

    Havruta study in pairs, each student reads a sentence and explains it to their havruta (10 - 20 minutes).

  3. 3

    Personal havruta study with an AI assistant + headphones with a microphone for every student (10 - 15 minutes).

About 30 - 45 minutes in total.

Examples of Talmudic texts that are used:

A Talmudic text as it is, in a pure English translation without any commentary.

How does it look on the original, authentic Talmud page?

How the artificial intelligence system measures the 3 skills:

In the AI havruta stage, the artificial intelligence assistant will serve as an almost-human havruta (similar to a voice conversation format with ChatGPT), which is trained very, very well on the sugya, while behind the scenes it gathers data such as how many good questions the student asked, how many good answers they gave, how much creativity they showed. The artificial intelligence assistant will also be trained to encourage the student to ask questions and to develop the rest of the skills.

These data are reflected immediately on the student's board at this stage, and at the same time are also passed on to the teacher's screen, which receives an accurate picture of a student and the pace of their progress in developing these skills.

How the system looks:

The design collaboration + localization format:

One day a week that includes a round of 3 pairs of students navigating and learning with the interface. How does it look?
Each time only one pair carries out a full learning process; at the beginning of the process the teacher only explains the three stages to them, and afterwards they move on to the process itself, in which the students begin learning while a laptop with Zoom open is broadcasting live, which lets us see the learning interaction, and the teacher is present with them passively and is responsible for reporting to us on Zoom about difficulties, or places where there was a mismatch, or a lack of understanding, or a need to improve something, or where the students get stuck at a certain stage, and is also responsible for reporting insights from the field to us after the Zoom.

The goal is to understand and make sure that we are adapting and designing the solution in the best, most useful and most suitable way for the students!

The pilot format:

In general, it can be said that the pilot format is intended for measuring the improvement of 3 main skills, which are:
critical thinking and asking questions, solving problems and finding answers, and creative thinking.

But at the moment it is a little early to determine with certainty what is right for the pilot format and for its scope. As an estimate only, it can roughly be assumed that it will take place once a week as a round of group classroom learning including about 6 - 10 students, for about 4 weeks, 4 sessions in total, + a laptop with Zoom open on the classroom + a teacher present in the classroom, responsible for reporting from the field and overseeing the process. The goal is to receive insights from the field, and to make adaptations and improvements from time to time.
